scores.evidence: Checked against the four sources in fixtures/northlight_01/. What works: every anchor resolves verbatim in its source (runs/tier3/harness_report.json T1.3, 17/17; I spot-checked the anchors in runs/tier3/brief.json). All three seeded conflicts carry every position with the right citations, including the four-position timeline conflict (brief.json conflicts[2]). The ten mandatories are complete and correctly cited. No budget total is invented. The TikTok dance stays conditional (brief_el.md:29). Open questions cover KPIs, approver, media budget, formats and the missing ingredient list (brief_el.md:52-90). The voreas rehearsal documents real synthesis defects honestly (runs/voreas_prep_report.md, findings 1-4 and addendum 1-6). Against that, the graded northlight run has several substantive defects that the frozen harness does not detect and that no document records.
defects: Garbled ASR tokens are corrected silently where readers see them. brief.json objectives[2] says 'Building brand awareness is central' and key_messages[3] says 'the key visual should evoke summer', both at confidence high. Neither render shows 'μπραντ αγουέρνες' or 'κι βίζουαλ' or any ASR flag (grep finds no hits in brief_el.md or brief_en.md). Harness T3.3 passes only because the garbled token survives inside the JSON anchor (eval/harness.py:481). The extracts also break SOURCES.md rule G ('confidence low'): extracts/transcript_kickoff.json objectives[0] and key_messages[2] carry confidence high.

Wrong source mixed into a citation. brief.json key_messages[3], rendered at brief_en.md:21 and brief_el.md:21, adds 'not a generic beach-party feel' and cites it to [transcript_kickoff 00:06:02]. The transcript never says this; it comes from background_brand_guidelines §Category no-gos.

Extraction translates, against SOURCES.md rule 5. extracts/transcript_kickoff.json key_messages[0] turns 'φυσικά υλικά' into 'natural ingredients'. key_messages[1] renders 'ελληνικό brand που κάνει τη μοντέρνα κατηγορία δικιά του' as 'Greek brand that owns the modern category (sparkling tea)', adding the parenthesis. deliverables[0] turns 'social stuff' into 'social content'.

The spoken budget figure drifts from the canonical wording. SYNTHESIS.md rule 2 prescribes 'around eighty (units unstated)'. brief.json conflicts[1] instead says 'somewhere in the eighties', which reads as 80-89. The same render then says 'around eighty' in open question 3 (brief_en.md:60 vs :102). The human resolution and edits_summary inherit 'production budget in the eighties', which is not a usable figure.

The signed-off brief contradicts itself. The Audiences, Timeline and Budget sections still read 'No confirmed entries' / 'Δεν υπάρχουν επιβεβαιωμένες καταχωρήσεις' (brief_en.md:15, :36; Timeline has no date at all). Open questions 2, 3 and 9 still ask the client things the account lead has resolved, e.g. 'No single confirmed audience definition exists'. The section titled 'Unresolved Conflicts' lists three items marked 'resolved by human' (brief_en.md:92-112).

Items are filed under the wrong field and useful facts are lost. 'Final approval of the brief' and 'Northlight will send a revised plan' appear as client deliverables (brief_en.md:24-25). The client's statement that it has no category research ('Έρευνα για την κατηγορία δεν έχουμε δική μας', emails M2) survives only as an extraction_note and never reaches the brief. The retracted metro OOH idea was dropped by the repair loop, not recorded as retracted (extraction_notes REPAIR line). That passes trap X1 but leaves the creative team with no warning.

Known defects are documented for voreas but not for the graded tier3 run. runs/tier_3_report.md records none of the defects above. The SYNTHESIS coverage rule queued in voreas_prep_report.md was never added (grep for garble/coverage in skills/SYNTHESIS.md finds nothing).
scores.to_reach_9: Make ASR normalisation visible in brief.json content and in both renders, with lowered confidence, and bring extract confidences into line with rule G. Remove the cross-source 'beach-party' mix-up and add a runner-side check that catches this class of error. Keep extract values in their source language. Canonicalise the budget as 'around eighty (units unstated)' throughout. After sign-off, fill resolved conflicts into their field sections (marked as human-resolved) and retire or annotate the open questions they answered. Add a 'known output defects' section to the tier3 evidence pack for anything that remains.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/brief_el.md and brief_en.md line by line against each other and against the sources, then sampled runs/voreas-prep-02/-03 brief_el.md and skills/TRANSLATION.md. What works: the section structure matches across languages. Brand-term fidelity is clean: 'Meltemi Fizz' always appears in Latin script and never alone as 'Fizz', and no 'Μελτέμι/Φιζ' exists anywhere. Glossary keep_latin terms (brand awareness, key visual, launch, media spend, KPI) are respected. Hedges transfer, e.g. 'Υπό συζήτηση — δεν έχει επιβεβαιωθεί' (brief_el.md:29). The Greek re-anchors to the source wording, e.g. 'να φωνάζει καλοκαίρι', 'κάπου στα ογδόντα'. The code-switching register fits the brand tone guidance. However, the Greek has enough grammar and word-choice errors that an account lead could not send it without a copy-edit. The Greek boilerplate is also regenerated by the model on every run.
defects: Greek grammar and orthography errors in a signed-off document: 'η θέση της προσώπου' should be 'του προσώπου' (brief_el.md:54); 'τη κατηγορία' should be 'την κατηγορία' (:68); 'τη τελική έγκριση' should be 'την τελική' (:86); 'Ποιό' should be 'Ποιο' (:66); 'και που ακριβώς θα χρησιμοποιηθούν' needs the interrogative 'πού' (:78); 'ορίζει το κοινό-στόχος ως' should be accusative 'το κοινό-στόχο' (:95).
Wrong word in the sign-off line. 'Επιλύθηκαν οι τρεις αντικρούσεις' (brief_el.md:115) uses 'αντικρούσεις', which means rebuttals. The intended word is 'συγκρούσεις' or 'αντιφάσεις'.

Calques and clumsy phrasing. 'Προγραμματίζονται κάποια videos και social content, κυρίως' (:28) leaves 'κυρίως' dangling, a calque of 'Some videos and social stuff, mainly'; the EN equivalent 'are planned, mainly' is equally awkward. 'Κάλυψη εισερχομένων' (:6), where 'εισερχόμενα' reads as an inbox. 'ποιος ορισμός στοχεύει το campaign' (:57). 'για τον σωστό scope της εργασίας' (:73). 'διαμερίζεται' (:62) where 'κατανέμεται' is the natural word. 'παραμένει ανεπιβεβαίωτο και παραμένει ανοιχτό' repeats the verb (:103).
Wrong time reference in a client-facing question. 'σήμερα ειπώθηκε' / 'today it was said' (brief_el.md:58, brief_en.md:58) is carried over from the 10 July call into a brief dated 24 July.

The two renders are not fully equivalent. EN key message 3 adds '(sparkling tea)' (brief_en.md:20). EN softens 'φωνάζει καλοκαίρι' to 'evoke summer' (:21). Inside the EN render, the same CFO figure appears as 'around eighty' (:60) and 'somewhere in the eighties' (:102). The latter means 80-89 and misrenders 'κάπου στα ογδόντα'. EL adds 'παραγωγής' to Eleni's 'αλλάζει αρκετά τον προγραμματισμό' (:33), and EN mirrors it with 'production planning'.

No fixed Greek boilerplate. templates/northlight_client_brief.md is English-only, so the model translates every Greek heading and label per run. Across runs the conflict heading is 'Ανεπίλυτες Συγκρούσεις' (tier3, voreas-02) or 'Ανεπίλυτες Αντιφάσεις' (voreas-03); the sign-off heading is 'Έγκριση', 'Υπογραφή' or 'Sign-off'; section 7 is 'Υποχρεωτικά & Απαγορεύσεις' or 'Υποχρεωτικά Στοιχεία & Απαγορεύσεις'. voreas-03 also leaves 'Verdict: ready_for_review' and the enum 'advertising_creative' untranslated in the EL header, and uses 'ολογράφως' (spelled out in words) where 'ολόκληρο' is meant, plus 'στέντ'. The tier3 EL title stays in English: 'Client Brief [EL]'.

Neither render is ready to send. Both carry internal metadata (sensitivity tier, pipeline id, readiness verdict), a section headed 'Unresolved' over resolved items, and questions to the client that the account lead has already answered.
scores.to_reach_9: Ship a fixed Greek boilerplate (headings, labels, banners, empty-section lines) so the model renders entries only. Add a deterministic Greek lint to the render self-check covering final-ν before stops, monosyllable accents, interrogative πού/πώς, and a short list of known wrong lexemes. Re-render tier3 and have a human copy-edit it, recording the edits in the signoff summary. Remove time words like 'today' from suggested questions. Make one canonical budget phrase hold in both languages. Split a client-send version without internal metadata from the internal version.

scores.evidence: Read runs/tier3/creative/creative_brief_sonnet.md and creative_brief_opus.md against brief.json, config/channel_specs.json, pipeline/creative.py:90-128 and runs/tier_4_report.md. What works: both drafts open with a SHADOW MODE banner. Both use the full eight-section structure. Both select spec rows from the table with row ids (sonnet :52-53, opus :63-69). Opus refuses to invent a YouTube spec ('SPEC NOT IN TABLE — ask traffic/production', :71). Sonnet refuses to assign Instagram when the brief names no platform (:54). The mandatories are reproduced. The TikTok dance is correctly kept out of scope. The readiness checklists are thorough, and opus sorts them usefully into blocking and non-blocking items. Opus's insight ('doesn't want to be lectured about health') is a genuine human truth anchored in the no-health-claims rule. However, both drafts invent facts, which is exactly what the stage claims to prevent, and tier_4_report.md overstates them as 'trap-clean' and different 'in thoroughness, not correctness'.
defects: Sonnet invents a unit and currency for the budget: 'Production budget: "in the eighties" (€80–85k)' and again '(€80–85k)' (creative_brief_sonnet.md:64, :69). The brief explicitly records 'no confirmed unit or currency' (brief_en.md:60). '€80' is the pattern trap X3 forbids, yet tier_4_report.md:66 calls both drafts 'trap-clean'.

Sonnet makes an unsupported market claim: sparkling tea is 'a category … that is new to Greece' (:9). The source says the category is new to the company ('καινούργια κατηγορία για εμάς', transcript 00:02:05).

Opus's SMP makes an unverified provenance claim: 'Meltemi Fizz is the Greek-made sparkling tea' (creative_brief_opus.md:11). The sources only say 'ελληνικό brand'. Where the product is made appears nowhere, and a made-in claim needs the same verification as any other product claim.
Opus says the TikTok dance was 'floated speculatively and retracted' (:73). It was never retracted; the retraction belongs to the metro OOH idea.

The sharpest strategic issue is missing from both drafts. The RFP's TikTok-first mandate was written under the Gen Z 18-24 assumption, which the CMO corrected to 25-40 urban professionals. Neither draft asks whether TikTok-first still holds for the resolved audience; both simply tell the audience to follow the brand on TikTok (sonnet :17, opus :25). Neither addresses the tension between 'premium summer' and a 15 September launch at the end of the season.

Sonnet's SMP is not single-minded: it bundles zero sugar, premium, everyday ritual and Greek ownership into one line. It also uses lowercase 'sugary, beach-party fizz' right next to the brand name (:5), which risks the 'never abbreviated to Fizz' rule and reads as a category jibe.

Specs are not reproduced byte-for-byte. Sonnet writes '9–60s' with an en dash (U+2013) where the table has '9-60s' (:52). check_creative_brief scans only resolution and ratio tokens (pipeline/creative.py:38-44), so durations and file types go unchecked. The claim in channel_specs.json that 'every spec-shaped token … byte-for-byte' is checked is broader than what is enforced.

Labelling problems. Opus's heading says 'Mandatories & no-gos (verbatim from the brief)', but it trims 'attached by Dimitris' and drops the RFP §7 mandatory (:49). The model itself wrote 'Reviewed by a creative lead for evaluation only' (:5), stating a human review as if it had already happened. tier_4_report.md:118 says the drafts are gitignored, but git ls-files shows both are tracked.
scores.to_reach_9: Add a creative fact gate: every number or currency token and every provenance or market claim must appear in brief content strings, and duration and file-type tokens must match the table byte-for-byte. Have the creative-shadow order require a 'strategic tensions' line that relates resolved conflicts to the remaining mandatories (TikTok-first vs 25-40; season vs launch date). Re-run the A/B and correct tier_4_report.md's 'trap-clean / thoroughness not correctness' reading with the verified defects.

moves.title: Fill human resolutions into the signed-off brief and retire the questions they answered
moves.rationale: The signed-off tier3 brief says 'No confirmed entries' for Audience, Budget and Timeline. It still asks the client three questions the account lead has resolved, and it lists resolved items under an 'Unresolved Conflicts' heading. This single contradiction is what most undermines trust for an account lead and a hiring panel. It can be fixed deterministically from fields already in the frozen schema (conflicts[].status, resolution, resolved_by).
moves.concrete_changes: In the post-sign-off re-render path in pipeline/stages.py (render work order) and in templates/northlight_client_brief.md: (1) when conflicts[i].status == 'resolved_by_human', render the resolution as the first line of the matching field section, tagged '[resolved by account lead — see conflict]' / '[επιλύθηκε από τον account lead — βλ. σύγκρουση]'; (2) make the conflict heading depend on status ('Conflicts & resolutions' / 'Συγκρούσεις & επιλύσεις' once all are resolved); (3) mark open questions whose field matches a resolved conflict as 'answered at sign-off' instead of rendering them as live client questions. Add tests in tests/test_stages.py for all three. Re-render runs/tier3 through the render stage, not by hand.

moves.title: Fixed Greek boilerplate plus a deterministic Greek lint in the render self-check
moves.rationale: The Greek headings and labels are model-generated per run and drift between runs ('Συγκρούσεις' vs 'Αντιφάσεις', 'Έγκριση' vs 'Υπογραφή' vs 'Sign-off'). tier3 also contains six to seven mechanical grammar errors (τη/την, Ποιό, που/πού, της προσώπου, κοινό-στόχος as object) that a small lint catches cheaply.
moves.concrete_changes: Add templates/northlight_client_brief.el.md (and .en.md) containing the exact fixed heading, label, banner and empty-section strings, and change the render order to pass the language-specific template. Add pipeline/greek_lint.py (runner-side, not the frozen harness) with: final-ν check for τη/το/ένα/αυτή/δε/μη before a word starting with a vowel or κ π τ ξ ψ μπ ντ γκ τσ τζ; accented monosyllables (ποιό, πιό); unaccented 'που/πως' directly after a question word or inside '«…;»'; a small wrong-lexeme list ('αντικρούσεις' in a conflict context, 'ολογράφως' for names). Run it in the render gate beside the glossary check, with tests. Add one line to skills/TRANSLATION.md §4 self-check. Re-render tier3.

moves.title: Make ASR normalisation visible and fix garble confidences
moves.rationale: The brief and renders silently turn 'μπραντ αγουέρνες' and 'κι βίζουαλ' into clean glossary terms at confidence high. The harness passes only because the garbled token is hidden in the JSON anchor. The extracts break SOURCES.md rule G (confidence low). The voreas run showed the same gap causing content loss, and its queued SYNTHESIS coverage rule was never added.
moves.concrete_changes: skills/SYNTHESIS.md: add the queued coverage rule plus 'an entry built on a garble-flagged anchor states the normalisation in content, e.g. "brand awareness (ASR-garbled in source as «μπραντ αγουέρνες»; glossary match, unconfirmed)", confidence at most medium'. Add a runner-side check in pipeline/stages.py: any brief entry whose anchor contains a token named in an extract's garble extraction_note must carry that token in content, and confidence must not be high. Add an extract-side check in pipeline/extraction.py that garble-noted items have confidence low (rule G). Re-run tier3 synthesis and render.

moves.title: Creative fact gate: no numbers, currencies or provenance and market claims beyond the brief; full spec-token match
moves.rationale: Sonnet wrote '€80–85k' and 'new to Greece'; opus wrote 'Greek-made'. These are invented facts in the stage that claims facts are never generated. The spec gate checks only resolutions and ratios, so an en-dash duration passed.
moves.concrete_changes: Extend pipeline/creative.check_creative_brief: (a) every currency mark or number-with-unit token (€, k, χιλ., %, digits next to 'k') must occur in some brief.json content, conflict statement or resolution string, otherwise it is a violation; (b) match duration ('9-60s', 'up to 90s') and file_type tokens found on '[spec: …]' lines byte-for-byte against the cited row; (c) add a short denylist of provenance and market-claim phrases ('Greek-made', 'made in', 'new to Greece', 'first in') that require a supporting brief string. Add tests in tests/test_creative*.py using the two tier3 drafts as regression fixtures. They must fail under the new gate as the drafts stand today.

moves.title: Require a 'strategic tensions' line in the creative-shadow order and re-run the A/B
moves.rationale: A creative team most needs to know whether the RFP's TikTok-first mandate, written for Gen Z, still holds for the resolved 25-40 audience. It also needs to know how 'premium summer' fits a 15 September end-of-season launch. Neither draft raises either question.
moves.concrete_changes: In pipeline/creative.build_creative_order (and .claude/agents/creative-shadow.md): add a required §8 sub-list, 'Strategic tensions for the creative lead', whose items each pair a resolved conflict with a remaining mandatory or deliverable it may undercut, cited to both. The model may pose questions only and must not resolve them. Require the SMP to express one idea in 20 words or fewer. Re-run runs/tier3 creative A/B and replace the drafts.

moves.title: Correct the published creative and brief evidence claims and add a known-defects list for tier3
moves.rationale: tier_4_report.md calls both drafts 'trap-clean' and different 'in thoroughness, not correctness', and says the drafts are gitignored although they are tracked. tier_3_report.md lists no output defects, although the beach-party mis-citation, the 'in the eighties' drift and the Greek errors are all present. Overclaiming costs more with a hiring panel than the defects do.
moves.concrete_changes: Append a 'Verified output defects (post-hoc review)' section to runs/tier_4_report.md listing sonnet €80–85k (:64, :69) and 'new to Greece' (:9), opus 'Greek-made' (:11) and 'retracted' (:73), and the en-dash spec. Change the 'differ in thoroughness, not correctness' sentence to reflect this, and fix the gitignored statement at :118. Add the equivalent section to runs/tier_3_report.md for the brief and renders (garble normalisation, beach-party mis-citation, budget wording, resolved-but-unrendered sections, the Greek errors listed in this review). Once moves 1-4 land, mark each item as fixed with the new run id.

moves.title: Runner-side provenance check for cited lines, covering cross-source mix-ups
moves.rationale: 'Not a generic beach-party feel' is cited to the transcript but comes from the guidelines. voreas showed the same pattern with 'hero video' cited to an RFP that never says 'hero'. T2.4 only checks that a tag exists and resolves, so both pass.
moves.concrete_changes: In pipeline/gates.py add check_content_provenance(brief, sources). For each brief entry, extract quoted phrases and distinctive content tokens (glossary terms, quoted strings, hyphenated compounds like 'beach-party') from content. Require each to appear in at least one cited source's text, or in the glossary as a translation of a token in that source. Apply the same check to each rendered claim line against the brief entry it renders. Wire it into the synthesis and render gates with a repair loop, and add regression tests built from the tier3 key_messages[3] and voreas-prep-03 deliverable 2 cases.

moves.title: Canonical wording for the spoken budget and no time words in client questions
moves.rationale: SYNTHESIS.md rule 2 already prescribes 'around eighty (units unstated)', but tier3 renders 'somewhere in the eighties', which reads as 80-89, and the human resolution inherited it. Suggested questions written on the call day ('σήμερα ειπώθηκε') go into a brief sent two weeks later.
moves.concrete_changes: Add to pipeline/stages.py synthesis checks: a conflict statement or content that quotes a Greek spoken number must render its English as 'around <n>' with '(units unstated)' when the source has no currency mark. Add to skills/SOURCES.md open-question guidance: 'suggested questions contain no time or place words tied to the call (σήμερα, today, χθες, εδώ); name the meeting and date instead'. Add a runner-side lint for those words in suggested_question_for_client. Re-run tier3 and, when re-signing, ask the account lead to restate the budget resolution as 'around eighty (units unstated), excluding media'.

overall: Checked as a Greek copy editor and translator against the four fixtures. The evidence discipline is real: citations are verbatim, conflicts are complete, mandatories are complete, conditionals are hedged, brand-name fidelity is clean, and the voreas rehearsal report is candid about its defects. The graded outputs are not yet at the level of a strong agency deliverable. The tier3 brief silently corrects garbled ASR terms in what readers see and cites a guidelines phrase to the transcript. After sign-off it still shows resolved fields as empty, as open client questions, and under an 'Unresolved' heading. The Greek render has about seven grammar and word-choice errors (της προσώπου, τη κατηγορία, τη τελική, Ποιό, που→πού, κοινό-στόχος as object, αντικρούσεις) and Greek boilerplate that changes from run to run. The creative drafts invent a currency figure (€80–85k), a market claim (new to Greece) and a provenance claim (Greek-made), and both miss the TikTok-first vs 25-40 audience tension. The tier 4 report calls these drafts trap-clean. Most fixes are deterministic, runner-side and cheap: fill resolutions into the sections, fix the Greek boilerplate and add a lint, surface ASR normalisations, add a creative fact gate, and correct the published claims.
